title: Exact semantic state-index query-time ceiling
question: How much query-time state-addressing work can be removed by precomputing an exact semantic index over a fixed persistent state pool?
hypothesis: H_index_ceiling: exact precomputation can preserve state-addressing recall while replacing the O(M) learned scan with O(1) query-time lookup, at the cost of O(M) index construction.

arms.name: exact_index
arms.intervention: build an exact semantic signature -> address inverted index once before repeated queries

arms.name: full_scan
arms.intervention: scan all state items with the REP-006 bilinear addressor on every query

endpoints.name: index_build_reads
endpoints.role: secondary — one-time state reads used to construct the index

endpoints.name: amortized_build_reads_per_query
endpoints.role: secondary — index construction amortized over repeated queries

decision_rule.condition: exact_index state_top1_recall equals 1.0 and full_scan state_top1_recall equals 1.0
decision_rule.licenses: the exact index is a valid upper-bound ceiling for query-time state-addressing cost on the registered synthetic task
the exact-index construction is invalid for the registered task

held_constant: same REP-006 semantic state task construction and opaque addresses
one persistent state pool is built once and queried repeatedly 256 times
full scan uses the existing bilinear semantic addressor without learning
index is exact and deterministic; no learned parameters are introduced
candidate program routing is excluded from this ceiling measurement
C5 and prior REP evidence remain frozen
